proposed_sentence: In T1, one successful native-input-supervisor versus actually delivered compact-packet pair used 720,840 versus 445,333 native input-plus-output tokens, with original reward 1 and supervisor completion in both arms; this control is distinct from the native Codex harness.

The observed T1 difference is 275,507 tokens (38.22%), while first coding-message bytes differ by 10.56% and coding tool calls by 13 versus 9; this sequential pair does not isolate a causal compression effect or establish general efficiency.

The final T1 candidate records one dialogue, zero expansions, and verified historical packet inputs, while its generic coding-input census remains unavailable; historical verification does not recertify post-publication source freshness.

Nine historical T1 attempts span different implementation revisions: six have observed passing outcomes and known usage, three retain failures with missing usage, and 2,523,452 tokens is only the known subtotal; a separately identified planned packet slot was uninvoked.

The earlier successful 278,471-versus-404,456 configured-packet comparison delivered native fallback, while later retrieval-reference attempts used 508,303 tokens for a failed control and 548,438 for a successful candidate whose exact delivery remained independently unverified.

The retained 565,786-versus-402,169 frontier lead preserves two passing outcomes but two timed-out exact-input audits; its 71 focused passes coexist with seven broader security-profile failures whose reachability on the measured path remains unresolved.

Transport and retrieval savings remain separate from source semantics: in an authored six-read session, compact references used 47,816 bytes versus 47,593 for native references, and one-read compact sessions added 633 bytes; no general inverse for arbitrary edits to a minified whole codebase is established.

T2 retains distinct successful native and indexed trials at 228,630 and 22,749 tokens, the earlier failed no-index trial at 194,494, and a fresh successful no-index trial, fix-code-vulnerability__2f3LChX, at 282,802 tokens, 131.818202 agent seconds, and 265.46191 setup seconds.

T2 records a local header-guard contract and template synthesis with one planning invocation and no coding invocation; preliminary eligibility abstention differs from later contract-candidate dispatch, and this narrow repair does not establish discharged SecurityIR obligations or full static analysis.

T2 materialization and observed completion do not close the separate publication-provenance gap: the selected outer receipt records pending_native_stop, and the final accepted-root owner receipt and finite validation counts remain unrecovered.

T3 preserves an earlier numerical native failure at 161,750 tokens and supervisor success at 291,432; the separate successful T4 native/no-index/indexed comparison used 113,883/358,492/333,973, and the three passing Grok source/metadata treatments report 1,310,764/1,621,661/2,452,634 without an explicit complete-usage flag.

T4 is an unadapted, unsupported learned-path diagnostic: its matched Source384 parent had zero target-training steps, four unchanged unverified predictions labeled fail_open_source_contract_unsupported, 105 unresolved obligations, and no Intent384 checkpoint; auxiliary usage, numerical retrieval, successor-state, and final-output gaps remain distinct from its observed passing reward.

T3 and the Grok cohorts independently retain zero target updates in their own records; distribution mismatch remains a hypothesis alongside missing output coverage, unsupported source grammar or logic families, retrieval/planning overhead, and infrastructure failures, and more training alone cannot repair an unrepresentable grammar.

Both final T1 arms invoked Intent preplanning before decomposition with fail_open_no_checkpoint; their local code-learning descriptors report 24 epochs on 358 samples but no holdout evaluation or formal-translation authority, so neither a qualified 384D domain deployment nor complete cross-IR reasoning follows.

The historical final population remains 32 cells with 9 useful completions (5/16 versus 4/16), and the separate 24-cell pilot retains 10 historical useful labels; unavailable usage in half the final population prevents a complete-cohort token total.

Fourteen heterogeneous lifecycle cases contain two admitted call reuses, both cold-audited, including a case whose teardown correctly fails; the older one-in-26 false reuse remains retained, and constructed scorer false admissions and supplementary rescoring do not retrospectively qualify the original scorer.

The two natural Requests cohorts each leave every arm at one accepted issue out of two and zero completed trajectories; simple retrieval/template controls match measured memory action reductions, so completed-trajectory cost and a learned-world-model advantage are not established.

Retained solver, circuit, publication, and recovery results remain scoped to their encoded statements and actual callers; acceptance/reuse theorem sketches are explicitly unmachine-checked, and missing evidence-algebra/header-contract files and #print axioms prevent a new claim of kernel-only runtime-checker correspondence.

All-enrolled outcomes and distinct source revisions remain visible; final consistent cumulative session counters are counted once, provider-specific cache/reasoning categories retain their declared semantics, overlapping clocks are not added, and unknown pipeline cost, billing, and authenticity remain unknown.

The retained PDF has 10 main-text pages against the requested maximum of nine; this audit performed no clean build, did not verify the official unmodified workshop style, and did not qualify the author-only package as an anonymous supplement.
